observations: Configured identity is combined with actual verified-email native passkey proof; original tenant, resource, support approval, owner and version checks remain in their canonical owners.

Enterprise qualification, sandbox mutations, SaaS settings writes and native support request admission check actual proof within the original physical database transaction. Current native sessions and user generation are pinned; pending erasure, wrong/missing/revoked/expired proof and non-passkey proof are denied.

A real PostgreSQL cell-row blocker makes sandbox creation wait after preflight. An independent native session deletion commits before the blocker releases. No binding commits. The existing native board-lifetime fence also participates; this race is not attributed solely to the new helper.

Native settings route tests use a trusted actor carrier with structural native proof rows, actual Express routes and PostgreSQL services. They qualify domain behavior, not cookie/WebAuthn verification. Current passkey proof permits settings/drain changes; stale proof permits current private reads but refuses mutations; deleted/weak/missing proof prevents effects.

Support routes preserve the full actor, support authorization uses actual database-clock approval expiry, and proof/scope checks repeat before commit including idempotent returns. An actually expired approval cannot be revived with its historical call timestamp.

The pre-fix sandbox test observes the session-label-only creation resolving rather than being refused. The fixture later gains native passkey preparation for positive cases; the negative request still deliberately removes its session ID.

The final domain run predates only an explicit async wrapper on the lifecycle read query. That wrapper preserves its already awaited query result; the final compiler checks its final source. Support changes do not alter any behavior exercised by the unrelated domain suites.
compatibility: No schema migration or dependency change. Internal operator support methods now take AuthorizationActor rather than a bare user ID. Non-SaaS settings behavior is retained and its original route/service suites pass.
limits: These are native domain/structural proof tests. Maintained real cookie/WebAuthn browser evidence is retained separately in native-passkeys-2026-10-24.
SaaS drain process state still applies after durable audit commit; this process-local effect cannot share the database proof lock. Durable drain state remains open.

Later runtime/host/provider dispatch and completion require their original operation, current-authority and unknown-outcome owners. Request creation is not dispatch qualification. Sandbox host-command requester provenance remains open.
Remaining runtime catalog/fleet/control, billing costs, agent package, feedback/retention and internal operator read owners, bootstrap and break-glass remain open.

Enterprise recovery/SSO, other powerful actions, original payload privacy/typed-origin/portability failures, full V10 acceptance and latest full workspace gates remain open. No PR-ready, beta, production, deployed replica or independent review claim.
